::: {.why}
A model with no inventory, no fees and no processing costs still produces a bid-ask spread, which is the cleanest possible demonstration that the spread is a statistical quantity.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Derive the bid and ask as conditional expectations given the direction of the incoming order.
- Say what happens to the spread as the fraction of informed traders rises, and what happens in the limit.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Derive it: with a binary asset value, a known fraction of informed traders and a competitive market maker who breaks even, the ask is the expected value given a buy and the bid is the expected value given a sell. Both are Bayesian updates, which is a calculation you can do in your sleep, and the whole model is those two updates.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Explore the mechanism: plot the spread against the informed fraction and show it diverges as that fraction approaches one, which is a market that closes. Then simulate the sequential trading and show the price converging to the true value, which is the model's other result and the reason it is called price discovery.
:::
:::
